newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Fourth bomb in week wounds 20 in Algerian cafe.
newsitem.headline: Fourth bomb in week wounds 20 in Algerian cafe.

text.p: A bomb exploded in Algiers on Sunday, wounding 20 people and bringing the toll from bombings in the capital to 18 dead and nearly 180 wounded in just under one week.
The earlier attacks were blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.
Algerian security forces, in a statement carried on the official news agency APS, said the bomb went off at around 10:30 a.m. (0930 GMT) in the southern suburb of El Harrach.
Witnesses said the bomb exploded in a cafe in the main square of the working class suburb, the third such attack on a cafe or shop in three days.
The independent newspaper Liberte said on Saturday that 12 people were been wounded on Friday when a bomb exploded in a cafe in the Moslem fundamentalist stronghold of Eucalyptus in southern Algiers.
Seven people were wounded in the blast of another bomb planted in a bakery on the same day and in the same area, El Watan newspaper said.
Two car bombs in Algiers earlier in the week were reported to have killed 18 people.

On Thursday a car bomb exploded near a paramilitary police station in Algiers, killing at least 10 people and wounding 68. And on Monday a car bomb ripped through the capital's commercial Larbi Ben Mehidi Street. The security services said it killed three people but local newspapers put the death toll at eight and said more than 70 were wounded.
Liberte said after Monday's attack that the rebels had made a mockery of government claims to have gained the upper hand in the war against the Islamic fundamentalists.

Until recently foreign diplomats in Algiers had described the city as relatively free of the violence that has gripped towns and rural areas, suggesting security forces had managed to keep the Moslem guerrillas at bay.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election that radical Islamists were poised to win.
